transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Collins (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Chen (Ketura Head of Infrastructure), Miguel Torres (Ketura Security Architect), Sana Rahman (Ketura ML Platform Lead), Jon Park (Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Ketura Health evaluating Redwood Private (on-prem, air-gapped) for regulated PHI workloads. Key concerns: offline update process, signed bundles, KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO artifacts, hardware constraints (rack power, limited PCIe lanes), model sizes and quantization, latency SLOs, cost tradeoffs vs Dedicated/Hosted. Next step: Redwood to share security pack and runbook; schedule PoC bench.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the ae on this opp, and ravi is our se, he'll jump into the technicals. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Laura Chen: good afternoon, thanks for making time. quick intro from our side - i'm laura, i run infra at ketura. miguel, sana, jon are on.
[00:14] Miguel: hi all.
[00:15] Sana: hey.
[00:16] Jon: yo.
[00:18] Ravi: great, thanks. quick agenda: understand your constraints (air-gap, hardware), what success looks like, and then go over redwood private options and offline update flow. sound good?
[00:26] Laura: perfect. our mandate: we must keep PHI on-prem, completely isolated from internet. vendor software can be installed but only via signed, audited bundles and an offline update process. we also have strict attestation requirements for cryptographic modules.
[00:38] Miguel: and we have limited rack space and power; we can't just drop a dozen h100s. current plan is 4 x A100 80GB per cluster, maybe one backup node. network is flat L2, no egress.
[00:50] Maya: ok, that helps. so you're looking at redwood private, correct? on-prem air-gapped deployment?
[00:55] Laura: yes. high level we want: model serving for clinical ingestion and triage workflows, latency under 120 ms for 512 tokens tail p95 would be ideal, throughput rough estimate 50 concurrent requests, variable seq lengths, and of course data never leaves premise.
[01:12] Ravi: good - those latency targets are achievable with model choice + batching. question: are you fixed on the 80GB A100s or flexible to L40s/H100s if we recommend?
[01:21] Miguel: procurement's slower. the budget is for A100 80gb but if redwood suggests an advantage to h100 we need cost justification. also PCIe power limits per rack is 16kW.
[01:33] Sana: also want to understand quantization implications - we run some bespoke models, not just open weights. can you handle nonstandard model formats?
[01:40] Ravi: yes, we onboard custom models. our runtime supports a variety of formats; sometimes we need minor conversion. for quantization we support int8 and 4-bit paths and can supply recommended profiles. one caveat: quantization and attention-optimizations can change latency/quality, so we'll run evals against your prompts.
[01:55] Laura: about offline updates - we cannot allow the runtime to phone home. what's your air-gap update pattern?
[02:02] Maya: good question. high level: we provide signed update bundles cryptographically signed by our release key. customers fetch the bundle via secure transfer (scp/usb), verify signatures, then install. we also provide an offline licensing/activation token that can be generated via a signed CSR exchange.
[02:18] Miguel: signature verification is fine; we need support for HSM-backed keys for signing and to integrate with our YubiHSM. can the update verification be performed by an HSM locally?
[02:26] Ravi: yes. verification can be gated by a local HSM. we also provide attestations for the binary (hashes), and we can generate SBOMs for each release. note: the on-prem control plane runs in your VPC, and the data plane never touches internet in the air-gap setup.
[02:40] Laura: what's the plan for security reviews? we require SOC2 plus ISO 27001 and evidence of pen test. do you have those?
[02:47] Maya: we do have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. we'll share the certs and a redacted pen test summary. we'll include the architecture diagram for the private deployment and our standard runbook.
[02:58] Jon: procurement will want an SLA and clearly defined patch windows. we usually push for a maintenance cadence that doesn't disrupt clinical ops.
[03:05] Maya: reasonable. we support configurable maintenance windows and can do an annual or quarterly patch schedule. for air-gapped customers we also support vetted emergency security patches delivered through signed bundles.
[03:15] Miguel: ok, what about telemetry? we can't ship usage data.
[03:18] Ravi: for private air-gapped, telemetry is optional. we ship an offline usage-reporting utility that you can pull and review; nothing leaves your network unless you explicitly push it.
[03:27] Sana: on performance: we need to run our internal RLHF-tuned clinical model - it's ~70B parameters. can that run on 4xA100s?
[03:35] Ravi: 70B can be tight. with FP16 and activation partitioning you might squeeze the model across 4x80GB depending on sequence length and KV cache. more likely we recommend model parallel setups or quantization to 4-bit. that's why we want your typical sequence distribution.
[03:48] Laura: sequence length is usually 256 tokens average, 1024 max in some triage cases. p95 latency target was 120ms, but we can relax to 250ms if quality is preserved.
[03:58] Maya: that's helpful. we should plan an initial bench with a 35B and 70B variant to measure both throughput and accuracy. can you provide a representative prompt set?
[04:07] Sana: yes we'll assemble a 500-prompt eval set that includes de-identified PHI-like content.
[04:12] Ravi: great. another question: how do you manage model artifacts - are models approved by internal governance team?
[04:17] Miguel: yes, models must pass privacy review and a 3rd party validation for hallucination thresholds. Also need a signed chain of custody for model weights.
[04:26] Ravi: we can provide checksums and signed manifests for the model files and tie them to the release bundles.
[04:31] Laura: on networking - no egress. does the installation require any external endpoints for license activation?
[04:36] Maya: no external activation required; we support offline license tokens signed by us that you can verify locally. optional: for customers that allow it we offer a small outbound egress for metrics, but you can disable it.
[04:47] Miguel: what about hardware drivers and container images? often our security team requires CVE scans of base images and kernel modules.
[04:53] Ravi: we deliver hardened images and will provide SBOMs and CVE lists for the versions we ship. for kernel modules and drivers, we can provide guidance but we generally rely on your OS/procurement for vendor-signed drivers (NVIDIA).
[05:05] Jon: cost question - on-prem vs dedicated: how should we think? we will own hardware capex but want software support pricing.
[05:11] Maya: typically private has a platform fee + per-node support and optional enterprise SLA. compared to hosted (per-token), private moves cost to capex. we can draft a TCO comparing 3-year hardware amortized + Redwood private fees vs Redwood dedicated hourly.
[05:24] Jon: good. include OPEX for emergency patches and on-site support.
[05:28] Maya: will do.
[05:30] Sana: do you support model split routing - e.g., smaller model for classification, larger for generation?
[05:34] Ravi: yes, routing policies are supported. smart routing can fall back to a smaller model for latency-sensitive calls. that helps cost and keeps p95 down.
[05:44] Miguel: about encryption at rest - we must use our KMS/HSM. can Redwood integrate with customer KMS?
[05:50] Ravi: yes, integrations for customer-managed KMS/HSM are supported. keys remain on-prem; Redwood uses customer key to wrap data keys. we support KMIP and PKCS#11 for common HSMs.
[05:59] Laura: any regulatory experience in healthcare?
[06:01] Maya: we have several healthcare customers running on redwood private and dedicated; we'll share case studies and references - redacted but relevant.
[06:09] Miguel: one more: attestation and image signing. we use secure boot and measured boot. can the redwood binaries be verified and included in measured boot policies?
[06:17] Ravi: yes, we can provide signed boot artifacts and supply the hash manifests for measured boot. we also support remote attestation if required but for air-gap you'll probably want local attestation against your TPM/HSM.
[06:28] Laura: what's the expected lead time for a pilot once we agree? procurement takes a while, but assume hardware available in 6 weeks.
[06:35] Maya: once hardware is available, on-site install + initial bench is ~2-3 weeks, PoC run 2 weeks. overall 6-8 weeks from hardware ready to pilot completion.
[06:45] Jon: procurement will need a scope doc and SOW.
[06:47] Maya: we'll draft a pilot SOW template.
[06:49] Miguel: regarding offline updates again - are we able to escrow signing keys or rotate signing keys periodically? we need key rotation without external contact.
[06:58] Ravi: rotation can be handled via staged signed manifests: you can accept a new signing key by checking a signed transition manifest that's included in the bundle and verified by the current key. for pure offline, you can also do a manual key-injection flow via your HSM.
[07:12] Sana: latency tuning - does the runtime support KV cache warm starts and checkpoint sharing across restarts?
[07:18] Ravi: yes, KV cache persistence and warm starts are supported. in air-gapped mode you can persist caches to local encrypted disk and we can give guidance for warm-up on restart.
[07:27] Laura: for the bench, we want to measure p50/p95/p99 for 256 and 1024 sequences, 50 concurrency. include both CPU fallback and GPU cases.
[07:36] Ravi: sounds good. we'll propose a bench matrix.
[07:39] Miguel: one security nuance: we need signed attestations of the kernel and the redwood runtime that tie to a particular version of the model. Is that possible?
[07:47] Ravi: yes, we can provide signed bundle manifests that include hashes for kernel, runtime, and model weights. you can cross-check before enabling the service.
[07:55] Laura: do you ship a control plane? how much of the UI is hosted vs local?
[07:59] Maya: in private deployments the control plane is in your VPC; dashboard UIs are accessible from your network. for air-gapped setups we provide a local console you can host behind your firewall.
[08:09] Jon: any dependencies on external artifact registries?
[08:12] Ravi: images can be mirrored to your local registry; we provide the image tarballs and manifests so you can import them offline.
[08:19] Sana: about model governance - can we lock model versions and prevent auto-rollouts?
[08:23] Maya: yes, you control rollouts and can pin model versions. automatic rollouts are off by default for private customers.
[08:31] Miguel: OK. in terms of acceptance criteria for the PoC: 1) p95 < 250ms for 256 tokens on 70B (or documented qual tradeoff), 2) model quality parity within X% on our eval set, 3) offline update verified via HSM, 4) full SBOM and signed manifests delivered.
[08:49] Maya: that's a good set. we'll draft a formal success criteria doc.
[08:53] Jon: finalize commercial terms later, procurement will want pricing tiers tied to number of nodes and support hours.
[08:58] Maya: understood.
[09:00] Miguel: any known limitations? e.g., drivers or kernel modules that would break in our hardened distros?
[09:05] Ravi: we test against common enterprise distros (RHEL, Ubuntu LTS) but if you run a heavily customized kernel we may need a compatibility check. we can run a pre-install checklist.
[09:17] Laura: ok, last question: disaster recovery - we need an air-gapped backup strategy for model weights and KV caches. suggestions?
[09:25] Ravi: recommended pattern: encrypted snapshots to removable media (tape/usb) with signed manifests; maintain chain-of-custody logs; periodic restore drills. we can provide runbooks.
[09:36] Sana: fine.
[09:38] Maya: great - recap of next steps: we'll send security pack (SOC2/ISO/pen test summary), air-gap update runbook and SOW template; ravi will draft bench plan; you will send hardware spec and eval prompts. schedule on-site week of 2026-12-08?
[09:52] Laura: yes that week looks promising.
[09:54] Jon: procurement will start paperwork.
[09:56] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.
[09:59] Miguel: thanks.
[10:00] Sana: thanks.

Notes on transcription: some product names were auto-corrected (e.g., KV cache spelled as K-V cache in audio), minor stutters removed. There are occasional mis-heard words in timestamps.

End of meeting.
